problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨3{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2,\,2{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the acceleration is
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2}-8t,\,6{t}^{2}-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9{t}^{2}-8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨18t-8,\,12t-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨18(1)-8,\,12(1)-2⟩ \\  & =⟨18-8,\,12-2⟩ \\  & =⟨10,\,10⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨10,\,10⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{10}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100+100} \\  & =\sqrt{200} \\  & =10\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=1\,\text{s}$ is $10\sqrt{2}{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$
